1	# Reading Sync Logs
2	
3	When you set `log.file: FULL`, pc-switcher records one line per changed item during a folder sync. Each line looks like this:
4	
5	```
6	/home/user: <f+++++++++ Documents/notes.txt
7	/home/user: cd+++++++++ Documents/
8	/home/user: <f.st...... Pictures/photo.jpg
9	/home/user: cL+++++++++ .bashrc -> /etc/skel/.bashrc
10	/home/user: *deleting   Downloads/old.iso
11	```
12	
13	Reading left to right: the synced folder, then an 11-character change code, then the item's path (with ` -> target` shown for symlinks). The change code tells you what happened to that item and why it was copied.
14	
15	## The change code
16	
17	The code has the form `YXcstpoguax`. The first two characters describe the item; the remaining nine describe which of its attributes differed from the target.
18	
19	### Character 1 — what happened
20	
21	| Char | Meaning |
22	| ---- | ------- |
23	| `<`  | the item was **copied to the target** |
24	| `c`  | a directory, symlink, device, or special file was **created** on the target |
25	| `h`  | the item is a **hard link** to another item |
26	| `.`  | nothing was copied — only attributes changed |
27	| `*`  | a message follows instead of a code (you'll see `*deleting` when an item is removed from the target) |
28	
29	pc-switcher only ever copies **from this machine to the target**, so you will never see `>` (which would mean the reverse).
30	
31	### Character 2 — the kind of item
32	
33	| Char | Meaning |
34	| ---- | ------- |
35	| `f`  | regular file |
36	| `d`  | directory |
37	| `L`  | symlink |
38	| `D`  | device |
39	| `S`  | special file (socket, pipe) |
40	
41	### Characters 3–11 — what differed
42	
43	For a **newly created** item there is nothing on the target to compare against, so every slot shows `+` (that's why new files read `<f+++++++++`). Otherwise each slot shows its letter if that attribute differed, or `.` if it matched:
44	
45	| Char | Attribute |
46	| ---- | --------- |
47	| `s`  | size |
48	| `t`  | modification time |
49	| `p`  | permissions |
50	| `o`  | owner |
51	| `g`  | group |
52	| `a`  | access-control list (ACL) |
53	| `x`  | extended attributes |
54	
55	(The two remaining slots — position 3 and position 9 — stay `.` for ordinary files in pc-switcher's sync.)
56	
57	## Worked examples
58	
59	- `cd+++++++++ Documents/` — a **new directory** that didn't exist on the target.
60	- `<f+++++++++ notes.txt` — a **new file** copied to the target.
61	- `<f.st...... photo.jpg` — an **existing file re-copied** because its **size** (`s`) and **modification time** (`t`) differed.
62	- `.f...p..... script.sh` — the file's contents matched; only its **permissions** (`p`) changed, so nothing was transferred.
63	- `.d..t...... Pictures/` — an existing directory whose **timestamp** was adjusted.
64	- `cL+++++++++ .bashrc -> /etc/skel/.bashrc` — a **new symlink** pointing at the shown target.
65	- `*deleting old.iso` — the item was **removed from the target** because it no longer exists here.
66	
67	## More detail
68	
69	These codes come from `rsync`. Their full specification is in the [rsync manual page](https://download.samba.org/pub/rsync/rsync.1), under `--itemize-changes`.

1	# VS Code State Sync
2	
3	`vscode_state_sync` selectively syncs each VS Code-based editor's (VS Code and its forks) global `state.vscdb` — the SQLite database under `~/.config/<Editor>/User/globalStorage/` — and the install-shared DB under `~/.vscode-shared/sharedStorage/`. These mix wanted global state (settings-adjacent values, MRU lists) with VS Code SecretStorage session blobs. The secret blobs live under `secret://` keys and are encrypted with a per-machine OS-keyring key that is never synced, so a plain file mirror would clobber the target's own decryptable secrets and force auth-backed extensions (GitHub, database extensions) to re-login after every sync. `folder_sync` excludes these DBs from its mirror (non-overridably); this job rebuilds each one instead.
4	
5	The job has no settings: the editor list, DB layout, and the preserved-key patterns are VS Code internals owned by the module, not things a user configures. Enable or disable it via `sync_jobs` like any other job; see the [configuration reference](../configuration.md#sync_jobs).
6	
7	## What the merge preserves
8	
9	The job mirrors every key from the source **except** the machine-bound account keys, whose value the **target keeps**. Two kinds are preserved: the `secret://` SecretStorage blobs, and the auth session preferences that point into them (`userDataSyncAccountPreference` and the per-extension `<extensionId>-<providerId>-<scopes>` keys). The pointers matter as much as the blobs — their value is a session id regenerated on every sign-in, so mirroring one hands the target a session it does not hold, and VS Code asks you to sign in again. Non-matched keys take the source's value; keys present only on the target and not matched are dropped (the same fidelity as the `folder_sync` `--delete` mirror).
10	
11	The preserved set is deliberately narrow: sibling keys holding the account *name* keep syncing (they are the same on every machine), and an extension you authenticate for the first time will not be covered until its key is added — it then asks for sign-in on the target once, rather than something you wanted synced silently going stale.
12	
13	`~/.config/Code/machineid` is **not** carved out. pc-switcher already mirrors Settings Sync's own bookkeeping, so keeping the machine id common makes the fleet one logical Settings Sync machine, which is self-consistent; splitting it would leave two identities sharing one machine's sync state. Consequence: the Settings Sync machine list shows a single entry for the fleet.
14	
15	## Coverage and execution
16	
17	Covered VS Code-based editors: Code, Antigravity, Cursor, VSCodium. Also covered is `~/.vscode-shared/sharedStorage/state.vscdb`, an install-shared state DB outside any editor's config directory (recent VS Code versions) holding cross-install state such as the workspace-trust list and recently-opened paths; it has the same schema and is merged the same way. For each covered DB, both the main `state.vscdb` and its `state.vscdb.backup` sidecar are handled identically — the exact set `folder_sync` excludes is the exact set this job merges, so no file is hidden from the mirror without being merged. A file absent on the source is skipped, and if the source has none of them at all the job reports **SKIPPED** — not applicable is not the same as synced. On a first sync (the target has no such DB yet) the target simply receives the secret-stripped database, causing a one-time re-login. The job runs after `folder_sync`, as the invoking normal user (no `sudo`), and needs `sqlite3` on both machines.
18	
19	Scope: this covers **only the invoking user** — whoever runs `pc-switcher`. If a synced `/home` contains other users, their VS Code state DBs are excluded from the mirror (so their secrets are never clobbered) but are not merged, so their VS Code global state does not sync. Multi-user coverage would require running the merge as root and is not currently supported.

1	# ADR-010: Standard Library Logging Infrastructure
2	
3	Status: Accepted
4	Date: 2025-12-31
5	
6	## TL;DR
7	
8	Use Python's standard `logging` module (without structlog) for all logging infrastructure, leveraging `QueueHandler`/`QueueListener` for async handling and custom formatters for JSON and Rich output.
9	
10	## Implementation Rules
11	
12	**Required patterns**:
13	- Register custom FULL level: `logging.addLevelName(15, "FULL")`
14	- Use `QueueHandler` + `QueueListener` for non-blocking log output
15	- Custom `logging.Formatter` for JSON lines file output
16	- Custom `logging.Formatter` using Rich for TUI output
17	- Configure logger hierarchy for 3-setting filtering (see below)
18	
19	**Configuration model** (3 settings):
20	- `file`: Floor level for file output (default: DEBUG)
21	- `tui`: Floor level for TUI output (default: INFO)
22	- `external`: Additional floor for non-pcswitcher loggers (default: WARNING)
23	
24	**Logger hierarchy setup**:
25	```python
26	logging.getLogger().setLevel(external)                    # Root filters external libs
27	logging.getLogger("pcswitcher").setLevel(min(file, tui))  # Let pcswitcher through
28	file_handler.setLevel(file)
29	tui_handler.setLevel(tui)
30	```
31	
32	**Forbidden approaches**:
33	- Do not use structlog processors or formatters
34	- Do not use custom async queue implementations (use stdlib `QueueHandler`)
35	- Do not create separate logging pipelines for internal vs external logs
36	
37	## Context
38	
39	pc-switcher's custom logging infrastructure (~180 lines) needs migration to capture external library logs (asyncssh, etc.) while maintaining configurable levels per destination. Initial analysis suggested structlog, but deeper evaluation revealed it adds abstraction without proportional benefit for this use case.
40	
41	See [considerations/adr-010-logging-infrastructure-analysis.md](considerations/adr-010-logging-infrastructure-analysis.md) for the full structlog vs stdlib comparison.
42	
43	## Decision
44	
45	- **Use stdlib `logging`** as the sole logging foundation
46	- **Use `QueueHandler` + `QueueListener`** for async, non-blocking output (replaces custom EventBus queue pattern)
47	- **Implement custom formatters** for JSON (file) and Rich (TUI) output
48	- **Use logger hierarchy** for 3-setting model (no custom Filter needed)
49	
50	**Why not structlog**:
51	1. `ConsoleRenderer` doesn't match our TUI format - custom work needed anyway
52	2. `JSONRenderer` adds no value over `json.dumps(dict, default=str)`
53	3. External library capture is native stdlib capability
54	4. Processor chain abstraction adds complexity without proportional benefit
55	5. ~15 line difference doesn't justify added abstraction layer
56	
57	## Consequences
58	
59	**Positive**:
60	- Simpler mental model - standard Python logging patterns
61	- Direct format control for TUI output
62	- `QueueHandler`/`QueueListener` provides proven async handling
63	- Easier debugging - standard logging semantics
64	- No additional abstractions to understand
65	- Aligns with Deliberate Simplicity principle
66	
67	**Negative**:
68	- Slightly more boilerplate than structlog (~105 vs ~90 lines)
69	- No built-in bound context (use `LoggerAdapter` or `extra` dict)
70	- structlog is already a dependency (remains unused for logging, may be used elsewhere)
71	
72	## References
73	
74	- [Logging Infrastructure Analysis](considerations/adr-010-logging-infrastructure-analysis.md) - Full comparison
75	- [Python Logging Cookbook](https://docs.python.org/3/howto/logging-cookbook.html) - QueueHandler pattern
76	- [Feature Spec 004-python-logging](../../specs/004-python-logging/spec.md)

198	    transaction — is never wrapped in the module's implicit DML transaction.

202	        connection.executescript(sql)

212	    and its ``libpython3.x-stdlib`` dependency carries the ``sqlite3`` module. ``uv`` is

217	    ever interpolated into the code Python parses.
218	    """

220	        "import sqlite3,sys\n"
221	        "con=sqlite3.connect(sys.argv[1],isolation_level=None)\n"

311	        for index, relpath in enumerate(present):

313	            target_db = (home / relpath).as_posix()
314	            label = db_label(relpath)
315	
316	            target_exists = (
317	                await self.target.run_command(f"test -f {shlex.quote(target_db)}", login_shell=False)
318	            ).success

320	
321	            if self.context.dry_run:
322	                self._log(
323	                    Host.TARGET,
324	                    LogLevel.FULL,
325	                    f"{prefix}Would sync {label} ({mode}); preserving keys matching {globs}",
326	                )

330	            await self._sync_editor(source_db, target_db, target_exists, globs, label)
331	            self._report_progress(ProgressUpdate(percent=int((index + 1) / total * 100)))
332	
333	        self._log(Host.TARGET, LogLevel.INFO, f"{prefix}{total} VS Code state DB file(s) synced")
334	        self._report_progress(ProgressUpdate(percent=100))
335	
336	    async def _sync_editor(
337	        self,
338	        source_db: Path,
339	        target_db: str,
340	        target_exists: bool,
341	        globs: Sequence[str],
342	        label: str,
343	    ) -> None:
344	        """Run the source-strip -> transfer -> inject -> atomic-mv sequence for one DB file.
345	
346	        Handles either a main ``state.vscdb`` or its ``.backup`` sidecar (same schema);
347	        ``label`` names which. The neutral DB is transferred to
348	        ``<target_db>.pcswitcher-tmp`` — same directory as the live file — so the final
349	        ``mv --force`` is atomic and preserves ownership/perms.
350	        """
351	        remote_tmp = target_db + ".pcswitcher-tmp"
352	        tmp_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="pcswitcher-vscode-"))
353	        local_tmp = tmp_dir / "state.vscdb"
354	        try:
355	            # Step A — source-strip: copy the live source DB, then delete preserved rows.
356	            # In-process: the copy is source-local, so no subprocess or shell is involved.
357	            shutil.copyfile(source_db, local_tmp)
358	            try:
359	                _run_sql(local_tmp, source_strip_sql(globs))
360	            except sqlite3.Error as error:
361	                self._raise(Host.SOURCE, label, "preserved-key strip", str(error))
362	
363	            # Step B — transfer the neutral DB into the target live DB's directory.
364	            # Ensure that directory exists first: folder_sync normally creates it, but
365	            # jobs are independently toggleable, so `folder_sync: false` + this job on a
366	            # target that never ran the editor would otherwise leave the SFTP put with no
367	            # parent directory. mkdir --parents is a no-op when it already exists.
368	            mkdir = await self.target.run_command(
369	                f"mkdir --parents {shlex.quote(Path(target_db).parent.as_posix())}",
370	                login_shell=False,
371	                mutates=f"create the editor state directory for {label}",
372	            )
373	            if not mkdir.success:
374	                self._raise(Host.TARGET, label, "state-directory creation", mkdir.stderr)
375	            await self.target.send_file(

377	            )

379	            # Step C — target-inject the target's own preserved rows, only when it has a live DB.
380	            if target_exists:

382	                    target_sql_command(remote_tmp, target_inject_sql(target_db, globs)),

386	                if not inject.success:

388	
389	            # Atomic replace within the same directory.
390	            move = await self.target.run_command(
391	                f"mv --force {shlex.quote(remote_tmp)} {shlex.quote(target_db)}",
392	                login_shell=False,
393	                mutates=f"replace the live {label} with the merged database, discarding the current file",
394	            )
395	            if not move.success:
396	                self._raise(Host.TARGET, label, "atomic mv", move.stderr)
397

1	# ADR-015: Topology-Based Sync-Safety Model
2	
3	Status: Accepted
4	
5	Date: 2026-07-01
6	
7	## TL;DR
8	Sync safety comes from btrfs pre/post snapshots (rollback backstop) + rsync `--dry-run` deletion log at FULL + a topology-based out-of-order warn+confirm step that reads sync-history `last_role`/`last_peer`; the btrfs `find-new` content-detection guard is removed.
9	
10	## Implementation Rules
11	
12	### Required
13	- Topology check reads `last_role` and `last_peer` from both the local and target sync-history to detect out-of-order sync patterns; on detection warn and require confirmation — never a hard abort
14	- Provide `--allow-out-of-order` to bypass the topology confirmation step
15	- Persist rsync deletion items at FULL log level for both `--dry-run` and real runs
16	- btrfs pre/post snapshots remain required as the rollback backstop
17	
18	### Forbidden
19	- No `btrfs subvolume find-new` guard in the sync path
20	- No per-target btrfs generation markers
21	
22	## Context
23	
24	The previous divergence guard used `btrfs subvolume find-new` to detect whether the target had changed since the last sync. Failures CR-01 and CR-02 (see `01-VERIFICATION.md`) exposed three root causes that make content-detection wrong for this use case.
25	
26	First, `find-new` answers the wrong question: it measures byte-changes since a given generation, not whether the target was independently modified by the user, which is the safety-relevant signal.
27	
28	Second, normal desktop activity — boot, login, cache writes, unattended upgrades — continuously bumps btrfs generations. Every path added to suppress this noise widens the false-negative window: CR-01 showed an unanchored substring filter silently masking nested user files, allowing `rsync --delete` to proceed against genuinely diverged data.
29	
30	Third, `/home` lives on `@home` and `/root` on `@`; a single `find-new` call cannot span the sync scope without reading two separate subvolumes, and the granularity of what changed does not align with per-folder sync semantics.
31	
32	rsync `--dry-run --delete` already provides the exact, scope-correct, noise-free preview of what would be destroyed, making content-detection redundant with the dry-run + snapshots combination and a permanent maintenance liability.
33	
34	## Decision
35	
36	- Sync safety rests on four pillars: (1) btrfs pre/post snapshots as the rollback backstop; (2) rsync `--dry-run` whose deletions are itemized in the FULL-level log; (3) a topology-based out-of-order warn+confirm step that reads `last_role` and `last_peer` from both the local and target sync-history; (4) trusting the user — no destructive-preview confirmation is required in the normal (in-order) case.
37	- `btrfs subvolume find-new` content-detection is removed. No per-target generation markers are maintained.
38	- The topology check is warn+confirm, never a hard abort: the pattern A→B / continue work on A / A→B again is a legitimate workflow (GitHub #159) and must not be blocked.
39	- ADR-014's "run divergence/conflict detection during dry-run" step is now realized by the topology out-of-order check, not by btrfs `find-new`; ADR-014 remains immutable and is not superseded by this decision.
40	
41	## Consequences
42	
43	**Positive:**
44	- Eliminates CR-01 (false-negative data loss from unanchored filter) and CR-02 (false-positive block on every upgrade+sync cycle)
45	- No per-machine exclusion denylist to maintain; the deletion preview is exact, scope-correct, and self-updating as the sync scope changes
46	- Topology check handles the safety-relevant case (unexpected source machine) without false positives from normal desktop activity
47	
48	**Negative:**
49	- Topology check requires populated sync-history on both machines; first-ever sync has no prior `last_role`/`last_peer` record (treat absent history as in-order)
50	- btrfs snapshots remain a mandatory prerequisite for the rollback backstop; the topology check alone is not a sufficient rollback mechanism
51	
52	## Refinement: first-sync is distinct from out-of-order
53	
54	This section refines the Decision above; where they differ, this section takes precedence.
55	
56	The original model folded three situations into a single orchestrator pre-flight gated by `--allow-out-of-order`:
57	
58	- W1: the target has no readable sync-history
59	- W2: the target last synced with a different peer (machine-C)
60	- W3: consecutive push — the same source pushes again without a back-sync (GitHub #159)
61	
62	W1 is not an out-of-order condition. A target with no readable sync-history has never been synced by pc-switcher, so there is no prior topology to be "out of order" with. It is a first-ever sync whose risk is simply that `rsync --delete` will overwrite everything in scope of the configured sync jobs wholesale. That is a different question ("do you want to overwrite this untracked target?") from the out-of-order question ("this target's last peer isn't who you expect"), and it warrants its own confirmation with its own bypass flag.
63	
64	Decisions:
65	
66	- First-sync is an orchestrator-level pre-flight check, not a job-level check. The orchestrator already reads the target's sync-history over SSH after acquiring the target lock; a job cannot cleanly obtain that signal, and the "first sync overwrites the target" question is common to all sync jobs, so it must be asked once centrally rather than per-job. Unreadable, empty, or unparsable target history is treated as a first sync.
67	- On a first sync the orchestrator issues an explicit "this overwrites the target" confirmation naming the in-scope folders (read from the folder_sync job config). Non-first syncs skip it.
68	- First-sync (W1) and out-of-order (W2/W3) are distinct gates with distinct flags, both in the orchestrator's pre-flight (`_check_out_of_order`, which reads the target history once and dispatches): W1 is gated by the new `--allow-first-sync`; W2/W3 remain gated by `--allow-out-of-order`. `--allow-out-of-order` does not bypass the first-sync gate, and vice versa.
69	- Under `--dry-run`, both gates log their warning and proceed without prompting (ADR-014: dry-run is a read-only rehearsal).
70	- A reusable `Confirmer` abstraction (`pcswitcher.confirmer.TerminalUIConfirmer`) backs both gates. Interactive runs pause the live TUI, show a yellow Rich panel, and prompt `Continue anyway? [y/n]`; non-interactive runs fall back to the caller's `--allow-*` flag. It is injected via `JobContext.confirmer` so future interactive jobs can reuse the same mechanism instead of reaching into the console/TUI directly. `FolderSyncJob` itself does not read sync-history or issue the first-sync confirmation.
71	
72	This supersedes the Consequences note "first-ever sync … treat absent history as in-order": absent history is now handled by the first-sync confirmation, not silently treated as in-order.
73	
74	## Refinement: peer hostnames are acquired symmetrically and compared case-insensitively
75	
76	This section refines the Decision above; where they differ, this section takes precedence.
77	
78	The topology check compares recorded `last_peer` values against the machines involved. For that comparison to be reliable, both peers must name the same machine the same way. Two rules make this hold:
79	
80	- Both ends record a machine's *own* hostname. The source records its peer as the target's `socket.gethostname()` queried over SSH (not the user-typed CLI argument, which may be an SSH alias or IP), the same way the source obtains its own hostname locally. This keeps the SSH/rsync connection address (the CLI argument) separate from the recorded identity.
81	- Peer comparisons are case-insensitive. DNS hostnames are case-insensitive, and history written before symmetric acquisition (or via a differently-cased alias) can hold either casing. Matching case-folded prevents a clean back-sync from being misread as a machine-C (W2) sync — e.g. a target that recorded its peer as `nomad` still matches a source whose hostname is `Nomad`.
82	
83	## References
84	
85	- ADR-013: rsync-over-SSH as user-data transport (transport layer this safety model sits above)
86	- ADR-014: Unified dry-run contract — its "run divergence/conflict detection during dry-run" step is now realized by the topology out-of-order check; ADR-014 is immutable and not superseded by this decision
87	- CR-01, CR-02: `.planning/phases/01-home-sync-mvp-user-data-sync/01-VERIFICATION.md` — concrete failure evidence motivating the removal of `find-new`
88	- GitHub #159: the A→B / work-on-A / A→B pattern that the topology check must not block as a hard abort
